instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor conducting a reassessment. Analyse the prior assessment summary, changes since last assessment, and updated survey, then respond with a complete reassessment JSON including score_delta, carry_forward, progress, and comparison_to_previous.

answers.companyDescription: Biotech company developing novel monoclonal antibody therapies for autoimmune diseases. Lead candidate in Phase II clinical trials for rheumatoid arthritis with promising biomarker data. 65-person R&D team. Key innovation need is AI-accelerated candidate screening using in-silico protein folding and binding affinity prediction. Multi-department organization with formalized budgets, quarterly business reviews, and a dedicated strategy function. We have invested in core systems (ERP, CRM, HRIS) but these are not always well-integrated. Innovation is a standing agenda item at board level with annual investment allocated, but execution velocity varies across business units.
answers.pastInitiatives: We have never run a formal innovation initiative. Problems are solved ad-hoc as they arise, usually by the most directly affected team member. There is no dedicated budget, no structured ideation process, and no track record of experimenting with new technologies or business models beyond basic operational necessity.
answers.strategicGoals: Customer retention has declined from 92% to 84% over the past 18 months, primarily among our mid-tier and enterprise segments. Exit interviews consistently cite product stagnation and poor digital self-service tools as reasons for leaving. We need to urgently modernize our customer-facing technology and proactively address the specific pain points driving churn before the trend becomes irreversible.
answers.teamSize: Our R&D function consists of 10-12 engineers organized into two squads: one focused on core product innovation and one on exploratory/new business model prototyping. We also have 2 dedicated data engineers building our analytics infrastructure. Innovation projects follow a lean startup methodology with clear go/no-go criteria at 3-month checkpoints.
answers.additionalContext: We completed a merger with a similarly-sized competitor 4 months ago and are in the middle of integrating teams, systems, and processes. The combined organization has significant duplication — two CRMs, two HR systems, overlapping product lines. There is a unique window to redesign processes from scratch rather than patching legacy approaches, but cultural integration is fragile and change fatigue is real.

input.changes_since_last: Regulatory changes forced compliance reviews. 7 new standard procedures implemented. Team morale improving.

opportunities.title: Redesigning the Customer Lifecycle Tech Stack for Retention
opportunities.rationale: The decline in customer retention (92% to 84%) is a critical market defense threat. Focusing on modernizing self-service tools and addressing product stagnation directly tackles executive concern. This leverages existing strategic focus while formalizing tech modernization efforts.

first_actions: Conduct joint user journey mapping workshops involving sales, support, and product teams (Merger necessity).
Audit current CRM/self-service tools against industry best practices for biotech client engagement.
Define 3 core high-value digital features that directly address cited pain points in exit interviews.
resources_needed: Stakeholder buy-in from the small leadership team
execution_plan.success_metric: Increase customer satisfaction score (CSAT) for digital interactions by 15% within 6 months.
milestones: Completed user journey maps and pain point inventory
Prioritized backlog of minimum viable product (MVP) features
Successful pilot launch of the first modernized self-service module

opportunities.title: Establishing a Formalized AI-Driven Innovation Funnel (Discovery to Pilot)
opportunities.rationale: While the technical capability for AI screening is present, the process remains ad-hoc. Structuring this into a formal funnel institutionalizes innovation and provides necessary rigor post-merger integration chaos. This moves beyond basic necessity toward proactive market leadership.

first_actions: Establish a dedicated 'AI Innovation Working Group' with representation from R&D, Data Engineering, and Strategy.
Define clear go/no-go criteria for screening projects (e.g., required biomarker correlation or potential IP value).
Allocate a small, protected budget (Proof of Concept fund) exclusively for computational biology experimentation.
resources_needed: AI Ethics and Governance framework (Compliance step)
execution_plan.success_metric: Generate three validated, data-backed hypotheses for novel target indications within 9 months.
milestones: Formalized intake process and criteria documentation (Process mapping)
Successful execution of first end-to-end AI screening project
Presentation of the top candidate hypothesis to the Board.

next_steps.action: Conduct a comprehensive Technology Stack Audit to map dependencies and identify immediate duplication points (CRM, HRIS) exacerbated by the merger.
Implement a mandatory change management communication plan targeting 'Change Fatigue' and reinforcing the value of structured processes across all merged teams.
Executive workshop to define a single, unified definition of 'Product Stagnation' and quantify its cost relative to retention decline.

key_weaknesses: Fragile cultural integration following the recent merger, hindering cross-departmental collaboration.
Reliance on ad-hoc problem solving; no formalized pipeline for converting scientific insight into commercial product strategy.
Deeply duplicated and poorly integrated core enterprise systems (CRMs/HRIS), increasing operational risk and cost.

improvements: Successful implementation of 7 new standard compliance procedures, showing commitment to regulatory rigor.
Digital maturity increased from Level 2 to Level 3, establishing core systems (ERP, CRM, HRIS) foundationally.
Improved team morale and engagement are noted, providing a positive cultural anchor point.
persistent_gaps: Lack of formalized innovation methodology; processes still rely heavily on key individual contributors.
Critical failure to harmonize merged technology stacks, creating operational drag and delaying strategic initiatives.
The commercial gap between scientific capability (R&D) and market execution (Customer Experience) remains wide.
achieved_milestones: Completion of key initial recommendations (opp_2 and step_1), confirming institutional process adherence in certain areas.
Formal allocation of annual board-level investment towards innovation, validating strategic commitment.

comparison_to_previous.key_changes: Increased digital maturity (2->3), implemented new compliance procedures due to regulatory changes, and achieved progress on key initial recommendations. However, the merger integration and persistent informal process gaps remain major risks.
